speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked the Minister for Education (Schools) (a) how prevalent and serious is bullying in our schools; (b) what preventive measures are undertaken to minimise and detect bullying; (c) whether our teachers are trained to handle bullying incidents; and (d) whether students involved in bullying and who are victims of bullying are given counselling care.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This is quite similar to the Ministry of Education's (MOE's) findings and other local studies.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: When students misbehave or make mistakes, schools will discipline and educate them so that there is learning and it will not be repeated.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Our school personnel have been trained to give attention to and address hurtful behaviours.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Teachers are provided with training in classroom management strategies and positive classroom culture.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: There are resources which provide information, strategies and good practices to instill good discipline.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Through Character and Citizenship Education, students learn social skills, empathy, respect and awareness of the effects of mean actions on others.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: They also learn coping strategies, relationship management and help-seeking skills.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Schools also actively create a positive and supportive environment for all our students.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: They have strengthened peer support by equipping students with relevant skills, such as befriending and active listening.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The peer supporters will alert and seek help from their teachers when they observe situations that affect the safety of their classmates.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There seems to be growing instances of people posting video recordings of bullying online which affect the students, the schools' reputation and the teachers' reputation, too.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, how does the Ministry respond to this?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, while the act is prohibited, the upstream measures that I have described actually are more important − teaching students how to cope with bullying behaviours, taking positive action to deal with those negative behaviours.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: And then, overall, in the classroom, how do you teach positive social behaviours like empathy for others, learning to care for others, beforehand?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: So, proactive measures are what we are doing in schools, and this would be the emphasis.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Incidents in our schools in terms of bullying are very few and have been relatively stable.

speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
text: At which point in time does the child's mischievous prank become bullying, and the kind of support that are given to students who have been thus identified, and, of course, how they are identified?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: It can be physical, verbal or psychological in nature.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Because a post can be seen by many people and be easily reposted by others online causing hurt to victims, we understand that this is a growing area of concern and the schools are dealing with this.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And further upstream, are there initiatives to involve parents in character-building and values-in-action education of students in schools?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Beyond that, we are also in touch with stakeholders in the community.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is there right now a national hotline that children who are bullied can call up?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Because, understandably, some children may have reservations about approaching their teachers, friends and parents.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is there a national hotline, and is there awareness of that hotline among all the schools?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I believe the Minister mentioned the Singapore Children's Society.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, I just want to clarify if there is awareness of that hotline across all schools.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, are there more bullying complaints reported from a certain school and, if so, then should an intervention be done with the teachers of that school, that sort of thing?

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: And especially for bullying, where oftentimes it is local, the best way to deal with it is through the peer network, teacher network, counselling network and so on.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Where there is a hotline, that would be a useful medium as well.
